requiredFindings.title: Selection variant identity depends on JSON member order and does not record the selector key
requiredFindings.location: render.py Renderer.run protocol loop: variant = pascal(frameType) + str(index) over alternatives.items()
requiredFindings.detail: Rust payload variants for selections are named FactBatch0/FactBatch1 and Unavailable0/Unavailable1 by the enumeration index of the alternatives object. JSON object member order is not semantically significant, yet reordering an equivalent input reassigns which alternative is 0 or 1. No generated artifact (wire.rs, wire.ts, render-result.json) records which selector value ('false'/'true', 'WAIT_NATIVE_CONTEXT_VERIFIED'/'ANALYZING') a variant belongs to. With the pinned input the alternative types differ, so a handwritten M3 decoder is protected by type checking. But the renderer accepts two alternatives of the same type, and then the index is the only, order-derived, discriminator. UNIT.md requires M3 to decode by frame tag plus admitted host selector, so the carrier must bind selector to variant deterministically.
evidence: baseline: FactBatch0(Box<Ts2FactBatchV1>), FactBatch1(Box<Ts2FactBatchV3>); no selector string appears in wire.rs payload enums or in wire.ts
Ts2 FactBatch alternatives reordered (true before false): render ok; variant 0 becomes the V3 alternative, TS rows reorder
both alternatives set to the same type: render ok, two rows/variants distinguished only by index
mutation D9 (swap indices) is caught only because the positive test pins FactBatch0 to V1, which in turn relies on input order
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Bind variants to declared selector keys independently of input order. Either derive names from the key (e.g. FactBatchFalse/FactBatchTrue, UnavailableWaitNativeContextVerified/UnavailableAnalyzing), or iterate alternatives in the renderer's fixed per-mechanism key order and emit the selector key per variant (doc comment or render-result mapping). Refuse or explicitly disclose same-type alternatives. Add a test that a reordered alternatives object yields identical output. Option 2 keeps current outputs byte-identical if the fixed order matches the pinned input.
